sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchant Acquiring and Clearing Service Provider (PSP)

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (national level; no sub-state corporate registry distinction for private companies)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Roman-Dutch civil law tradition fused with English common law, subject to constitutional supremacy)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Acts 16 and 17 of 2024, read with the Companies Regulations 2011; sections 12, 13, 14, 15, 19, 23, 66, 70 and 90 are the operative provisions for incorporation, legal personality, registered office, board authority, first resolutions and audit appointment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), 77 Meintjies Street, Sunnyside, Pretoria, 0002; all filings are transmitted electronically through the CIPC e-Services portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1A standard or CoR 14.1B supplementary); the CIPC issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3) upon successful registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: South African law imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a private company. Shares are issued as no-par value shares and consideration may be nominal, subject to the section 4 solvency and liquidity test. No escrow account or capital deposit is statutorily mandated for incorporation. However, the South African Reserve Bank payment system designation process may impose prudential capital requirements at the licensing stage. Share subscription proceeds must be held in a FICA-verified corporate bank account opened immediately after incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Memorandum of Incorporation filed with the CIPC is adopted, and that 1,000 no-par-value ordinary shares be allotted and issued to the founding shareholders at a subscription price of ZAR 0.01 per share, subject to the section 4 solvency and liquidity test. RESOLVED that the registered office be 15 Fricker Road, Illovo, Johannesburg, 2196, and that the company secretary lodge Form CoR 21.1. RESOLVED that [Founder A] and [Founder B] are confirmed as first directors; [Founder A] is appointed Managing Director of the cross-border payment gateway business. RESOLVED that [Practitioner] is appointed Company Secretary, and the directors are authorised to open bank accounts, appoint an auditor under section 90, and apply for all regulatory authorisations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Optional name reservation and availability search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit one to three preferred company names through CIPC e-Services; pay the statutory naming fee per candidate; verify availability against the register of protected and offensive names; retain the name reservation certificate for transfer to the company upon incorporation. Name reservation is optional because a company may also be incorporated with a registration number as its name, but reservation is recommended for a branded cross-border payment gateway.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application in the CIPC e-filing module
Certified identity documents (SA ID or passport) of proposed incorporators and directors
Proof of name-search fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, undesirability or conflict with a protected name, file an objection or appeal through the CIPC name tribunal, or reserve an alternative name immediately; ensure the approved reservation is not allowed to lapse before the incorporation filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and first directors; external corporate counsel; notarial execution is not mandatory for a private company MOI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the MOI in standard (CoR 14.1A) or supplementary (CoR 14.1B) form. Include the no-par-value share structure, board composition, quorum and voting rules, director conflict-of-interest procedures, and any special conditions required for the future payment system operator licence such as enhanced disclosure duties and annual audited financial statements. All incorporators must sign the MOI and any supplementary provisions before lodgement.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1A or CoR 14.1B
Draft MOI approved by all incorporators
Pre-incorporation agreement or founders' consensus statement, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend and re-execute the MOI before lodgement if CIPC or counsel identifies omissions; after registration, a supplementary MOI amendment under section 16 may be filed with director and shareholder resolutions to cure any defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of Notice of Incorporation and issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal; Companies Registry at CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload Form CoR 14.1 with the signed MOI, director consent forms and certified identity documents; complete the electronic declaration of the incorporators; pay the incorporation fee online; retain the CIPC acknowledgement. The CIPC will issue the Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3) once the filing passes statutory review, confirming the company's legal personality under section 19 of the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation)
Form CoR 14.1A or CoR 14.1B (Memorandum of Incorporation)
Consent to serve as first directors
Certified identity documents of incorporators and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a request for information or rejects the application, respond within 20 business days with corrected documents; use the CIPC correction window to rectify technical defects; escalate to the CIPC contact centre or an accredited registration agent if the query persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation governance filings, beneficial ownership and auditor appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC; Independent Regulatory Board for Auditors (IRBA); first board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form CoR 21.1 notifying the registered office and postal address. File the beneficial ownership schedule with CIPC as required by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 and the Companies Act section 56B. Appoint an auditor or independent reviewer in accordance with section 90; a payment gateway under SARB/FSCA supervision will require a registered auditor. Adopt a board charter, conflicts-of-interest register and annual financial statements cycle.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 21.1 (registered office notification)
Beneficial ownership schedule with individual details and percentage interests
Auditor or independent reviewer letter of acceptance
Board charter, director declarations and conflict-of-interest register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify CIPC compliance reminders on beneficial ownership within the prescribed 10-15 business days; if the appointed auditor withdraws, make a new appointment at an immediate board meeting and file the change with CIPC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS tax registration for income tax and ancillary taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax through SARS eFiling and obtain an income tax reference number. Apply for VAT registration once the R1 million turnover threshold is exceeded, or voluntarily given the cross-border services profile; register for PAYE, UIF and SDL when employees are appointed. Complete the SARS registration within 21 days of incorporation or of the relevant liability event.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3)
Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified identity documents and SARS letters of directors
Bank account confirmation
Statement of anticipated turnover and payroll projections
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the registration or creates duplicate records, file a corrected registration through eFiling and engage the SARS taxpayer compliance desk to merge the reference numbers; provide additional business-model narrative for the PSP classification if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening and FICA client onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank of choice, e.g. Standard Bank, FirstRand or Absa, acting through the FICA compliance and client acceptance unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificate of Incorporation, MOI, first board resolution and beneficial ownership register to the bank; complete the client acceptance and risk-rating questionnaire reflecting the high-risk PSP business model; define mandated signatories and segregation of duties; submit to the bank's enhanced due diligence process, which may require a source-of-funds declaration and projected transaction volumes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3)
Notice of registered office (CoR 21.1)
First board resolution authorising bank mandates
Certified identity documents and proof of residential address of directors
Beneficial ownership statement and organisational structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further FICA documentation or declines onboarding, supplement the file with audited financial projections, board minutes on AML/CFT controls, and written evidence of the SARB designation application; escalate to the bank's regulatory compliance team or select an alternative licensed bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Payment System Department (NPSD) of the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) as the industry licensing authority, with the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) for conduct supervision; municipal Fire and Building Control authorities for physical premises clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Designation or Authorisation as a Payment System Operator and Third-Party Payment Provider under section 3 of the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998, read with the Financial Sector Regulation Act 9 of 2017 and transitional provisions of the Conduct of Financial Institutions (COFI) framework; no separate municipal business licence is statutorily required for an office-based payment service provider, but zoning approval and occupation certificates remain mandatory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), with the relevant provincial department, e.g. the Gauteng Department of Agriculture and Rural Development and Environment, as the delegated competent authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment under the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations, 2014 (GN R982-GN R985); Listing Notice 1 (GN R983) Activities 26 and 27 threshold applies to the office and data-hosting premises with standby generators below 10 MW; no full Scoping and Environmental Impact Assessment Report is triggered for a purely service-based payment processing unit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Municipal trade effluent consent (e.g. Johannesburg Water) with sewer discharge limits of pH 5.5-12.5, COD not exceeding 1,000 mg/L and TSS not exceeding 500 mg/L; standby diesel generator emissions must comply with the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 and the National Dust Control Regulations, with a PM10 limit of 300 ug/m3 daily average at the boundary; e-waste and server decommissioning subject to the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 duty-of-care, hazardous waste manifests and WEEE compliance protocols.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety and Occupation Certificate issued by the municipal Fire and Rescue Service under the National Building Regulations and SANS 10400 Part T; electrical Installation Certificate of Compliance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993; structural load approval for server rooms under SANS 10400 Parts A and B; occupational health and safety workplace clearance for the open-plan IT environment; letter of good standing under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA); emergency evacuation and business-continuity plan filed with the municipal disaster management centre.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – National portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned South African company must register as a taxpayer with SARS via eFiling or at a SARS branch. The process includes completing the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) registration, then SARS registration for Income Tax (ITREF number) and VAT (VAT vendor number). Required documents include the company registration certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, directors' identity documents, and proof of registered office address. For non-resident directors, additional supporting evidence and a local representative taxpayer are typically mandated.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (South African resident company subject to corporate income tax; foreign-controlled entities may be subject to controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution under s9D of the Income Tax Act); Territorial scope limited to source-based and residence-based rules (worldwide income for SA residents, SA source income for non-residents).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general 'check-the-box' regime; entity classification follows statutory legal form (Pty Ltd is inherently taxed as a company). Hybrid mismatch elections are limited to specific anti-avoidance rules under s8B–s8I of the Income Tax Act (OECD Hybrids rules) and require formal disclosure and IRS/SARS alignment, but are not 'elections' in the US sense. Foreign tax credit elections and group relief elections (s45, s41) may apply to qualifying MNE groups.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration when taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month period; voluntary registration threshold is ZAR 50,000 for commercial entities. A non-resident supplying electronic services to SA recipients may be required to register irrespective of threshold if supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 per annum (VAT Act s50A).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance or a government-API e-invoicing stamp. However, all VAT returns must be submitted electronically via SARS eFiling or an integrated API. SARS has formally announced a phased mandatory e-invoicing framework (per SARS Strategic Plan 2025/26), but no in-force digital stamping requirement exists as of the current tax year. VAT invoices must reflect SARS-prescribed fields and be retained in original electronic form.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the export of movable goods supplied to non-residents and conventionally exported from South Africa within 28 days of supply (VAT Act s11(1)(a)). Exported services qualify if the services are supplied to a non-resident and are not consumed in South Africa (s11(2) read with s11(3)). Cross-border payment gateway services are, however, typically exempt financial services under s12(a) unless specifically made zero-rated by the Minister, so PSPs must carefully document the nature of each fee stream and require supporting evidence from the foreign counterparty.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 / SAD501) as per Customs and Excise Act
Bill of Lading (sea) or Airway Bill (air) evidencing export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT confirmation showing foreign settlement
Commercial invoice and contract showing supply to a non-resident
Proof of export within 28 days (port shipping schedule, customs clearance notice)
Proof of service consumption outside South Africa for offshore services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS will disallow zero-rating if the exporter has not received the exported goods' proceeds within 180 days (unless extended by the South African Reserve Bank under exchange control). Erroneous or fraudulent zero-rating triggers a VAT assessment at 15% plus interest under s89(2) of the VAT Act and the Tax Administration Act; understatement penalties may reach 150% of the additional tax in cases of 'substantial understatement' or intentional tax evasion (TAA s223). Criminal prosecutions for fraud carry fines up to ZAR 30,000 per offence or imprisonment up to 24 months, and directors may be held personally liable under CIPC/SARS joint enforcement. Retrospective clawbacks may be raised for the preceding 5 years (or 10 years for intentional non-disclosure).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933; the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961; and the SARB Exchange Control Manual, as delegated by the Minister of Finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a partially convertible capital account with a liberalised current account. The rand (ZAR) is freely usable for bona-fide trade, services, interest, royalties and profit remittances where the underlying transaction is properly documented and effected through an Authorised Dealer. Inward non-resident capital flows (equity and qualifying shareholder loans) are generally permitted without prior FinSurv approval, but the inward remittance must be reported to the Authorised Dealer and recorded in the bank's Exchange Control Management system. Dividends and profits may be remitted to non-residents without separate exchange-control approval provided the remittance is funded from audited after-tax profits, withholding/dividends tax has been paid or declared, and the initial capital import was endorsed. The practical profit-remittance hurdle is evidencing source of funds, proving the after-tax profit calculation, and ensuring that the capital was originally admitted through the formal banking channel with a Certificate of Capital Import obtained at that time.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation 3 and FinSurv rulings, exporters of goods must receive full payment in a freely convertible currency within 180 days from date of shipment. Payment must be received through an Authorised Dealer in South Africa and must be surrendered, meaning sold into ZAR or credited to an SARB-approved Foreign Currency Account held with that Authorised Dealer. The mandatory surrender/conversion ratio is 100% of the export proceeds; no residual offshore retention, netting, or set-off is permitted unless specifically approved by FinSurv. Extensions beyond 180 days can only be granted through the Authorised Dealer within its delegated discretion or by FinSurv for exceptional structured trade and project-finance receivable tenors. For a cross-border payment gateway not exporting physical goods, the equivalent compliance obligation is that all merchant settlement and cross-border payment revenues must be repatriated and cleared through an Authorised Dealer, with the same 180-day documentary discipline applied to underlying trade transactions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
First National Bank (a division of FirstRand Bank Limited)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM, with strict legal constraints. South Africa does not yet provide a domestic 'Electronic Money Institution' licence equivalent to the EU/UK EMI regime. Non-bank payment service providers require registration under the National Payment System Act and are not Authorised Dealers under exchange control. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, or similar digital banks cannot operate independently as South African clearing and settlement members, and cannot open ZAR nostro accounts with local clearing participation. Any merchant payout or cross-border transfer that bypasses a registered Authorised Dealer exposes the entity to exchange-control prosecutions. The legally viable fintech structure is to contract with a licensed South African PSP/PISP or Banking-as-a-Service provider that has a sponsorship agreement with a Tier-1 bank; the bank remains the settlement sponsor and exchange-control reporting agent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Bank policy and the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) require identification and verification of all beneficial owners and directors before account opening. Physical presence is not absolutely mandated by statute, but South African Tier-1 banks, when confronted with a high-risk cross-border payment gateway, invariably require at least one director and the designated AML Compliance Officer to attend an in-person onboarding interview at the bank's head office or designated corporate branch. The bank will also expect a physical or independently audited verification of the business premises and a walk-through of the transaction processing environment. Fully remote-only onboarding will normally be declined for an MVTS/PSP account. Once the account is established, periodic due diligence updates and remote meetings are permitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business classification as a Money or Value Transfer Service (MVTS) / Cross-Border Payment Service Provider, which is FATF-recognised as a high-risk money-laundering sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide FIC registration or required PSP/FSP licence, the entity's complete AML/CTF policy, independent AML audit or certification, sanctions and PEP screening software details, employee training register, and a risk-rating methodology demonstrating tiered merchant and corridor risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque beneficial ownership, especially non-resident shareholders, trust-based structures, or multi-tier holding chains.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the certified beneficial-ownership register required under the Companies Act 2008; notarised passport copies and proof of residential address for every natural person UBO; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds affidavits; bank references from the UBOs' primary banks; and a South African legal opinion confirming that no nominee, shell, or concealed ownership arrangement exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High expected third-party payout velocity to unrelated merchant beneficiaries, creating potential layering and trade-money-laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver executed merchant agreements, transaction flow diagrams, payout and refund procedures, merchant underwriting and rejection criteria, daily throughput limits by risk tier, and evidence of an automated transaction monitoring system with alerts and escalation workflow; commit to ISO 20022 enhanced data carriage and full audit levelling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Planned cross-border payment corridors into FATF grey-listed or higher-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a documented jurisdiction risk matrix, automated sanctions screening against UN, EU, UK, OFAC and South African domestic lists, prohibition of unlicensed counterparties, board-level approval requirements for high-risk corridors, Enhanced Due Diligence files on all merchants in those corridors, and a policy of regular financial intelligence reporting to the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All non-resident inbound capital injections for the South African (Pty) Ltd must be routed exclusively through an Authorised Dealer bank via standard SWIFT MT103 wire transfer and cannot be executed through cryptocurrency, foreign exchange bureaux, or offshore EMI accounts. The protocol is: (1) execute signed board resolutions, share subscription agreements, or loan agreements reflecting the exact funding amount; (2) instruct the sending bank to remit to the entity's ZAR domestic account held at the approved Authorised Dealer, using an exchange-control purpose code for 'Inward Equity Subscription' or 'Foreign Shareholder Loan'; (3) provide the receiving bank with the entity's registered name, Companies Act registration number, SARS tax reference, and the source-of-funds evidence from the sending bank; (4) the Authorised Dealer will validate the underlying documentation, confirm beneficial ownership, perform FICA due diligence, and issue a Certificate of Capital Import or non-resident capital endorsement in the bank's Exchange Control Management system; and (5) retain this certificate permanently to support future dividend repatriation, interest payments, and permitted capital reduction remittances. For shareholder loans, transfer pricing and thin capitalisation documentation under Section 23N of the Income Tax Act must also be prepared.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement and merchant payouts must be executed through the Authorised Dealer's clearing infrastructure. The primary rails are: SWIFT MT103 for individual cross-border beneficiary payments with full payment details and SARB-inspectionable purpose codes; SWIFT MT202 cover transfers for nostro funding where the customer instruction is to be credited through the bank's own correspondent account; and commercial documentary letters of credit (UCP600) where the payment gateway supports underlying goods trade against title documents, although an LC is not the ordinary clearing rail for pure online merchant acquiring. Domestic ZAR liquidity and instantaneous merchant payouts should be handled through the South African Multiplexed Overlay System (SAMOS) for large-value critical payments, the Automated Clearing Bureau (ACB) for low-value batch payments, and PayShap for immediate payment services. The treasury must maintain prefunded merchant settlement pools or a committed intraday overdraft facility with the Authorised Dealer to manage float and avoid breaching National Payment System Act clearing windows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts (FECs) with an Authorised Dealer, covering only genuine transactional receivables and payables
Spot-for-forward swap contracts and forward rollovers on ZAR/foreign currency exposure, executed through a registered Authorised Dealer
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-dated shareholder loans, nostro funding, or matched asset-liability treasury positions
Currency options (long call or put protection) purchased from a registered Authorised Dealer or offshore bank permitted under FinSurv approval

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currency legs that are restricted or non-deliverable, or as an offshore overlay hedge, provided the transaction is executed transparently through an Authorised Dealer and is not speculative
JSE-listed ZAR/USD currency futures and options exchanged under the Financial Markets Act, with no physical settlement outside South Africa

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 71 of 2008, s.33)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of ZAR 500 per month; omission for two consecutive years triggers compulsory deregistration/strike-off under s.82(1)(b).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be filed annually together with the CIPC Annual Return; any change of beneficial ownership must be filed within 5 business days after the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be fined or imprisoned for non-compliance; CIPC may refuse to accept the annual return; continued default contributes to deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of each financial year, as per the SARS-gazetted annual deadline for corporate taxpayers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative monthly penalty under Tax Administration Act s.210; criminal prosecution for persistent default; late payment interest on outstanding tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and compliance report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) Payment Services Division / Prudential Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end, pursuant to National Payment System Act licence conditions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Regulatory penalty or fine, and potential suspension or revocation of the payment service provider licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A company must have audited annual financial statements if its Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more, or if it is a public or state-owned company. A payment service provider licensed by SARB must always be audited as a regulatory licence condition, regardless of PIS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in South Africa; eligible private companies may apply IFRS for SMEs per the Companies Regulations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and file an annual beneficial ownership declaration with CIPC simultaneously with its annual return. Any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be updated in the register and filed with CIPC within 5 business days after identification. The declaration must disclose all natural persons with direct or indirect ownership, voting, or control of the company.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–800 per year (registered office and company secretarial services)

stage_6.entry_description: Company name, registration number at CIPC, and tax reference number
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not appear in the return; the company files as a South African tax resident; if the place of effective management shifts offshore, the company must notify SARS and may cease SA tax residence.
